investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T09:32–09:40Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no existing pod can be evicted to free capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector rules. The eval pod therefore remained Unschedulable for ~142–147 seconds until the probe timed out, preventing agent creation and producing an empty evidence object. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this evidence alone.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource fully consumed on both eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots on the 2 kata-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, and preemption found no evictable victims. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules. If those rules recently became more restrictive, previously schedulable nodes may now be excluded, effectively shrinking the eligible pool.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same 2 kata nodes simultaneously, capacity exhaustion becomes likely even without a configuration change.
Lower probability — eval runner submitting a pod spec with an incorrect or overly large kata.peerpods.io/vm resource request quantity, consuming more slots per pod than intended.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T09:32–09:40Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no existing pod can be evicted to free capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector rules. The eval pod therefore remained Unschedulable for ~142–147 seconds until the probe timed out, preventing agent creation and producing an empty evidence object. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this evidence alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T09:35–09:40Z because every pod submitted to provision a remote agent VM was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected because agent creation never succeeded, so the runtime response contract could not be exercised at all.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" was returned for all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) within the same ~5-minute window, and preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never returned a live agent, and all downstream evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) remained absent. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer, not a code defect or eval configuration error. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-layer failure.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval-provisioned agents. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — transient cluster-wide resource pressure or a concurrent workload spike consuming all peer-pod slots simultaneously: the three checks ran sequentially within ~5 minutes and all hit the same exhaustion state, suggesting the condition persisted across the entire window rather than being a momentary blip.

LOW PROBABILITY — eval runner credential or configuration issue: run-status-probes.mjs line 1915 guards on args.token; if the token were absent the check would return SKIP, not fail with a scheduler message. The scheduler message proves the API call reached the cluster, ruling this out as the primary cause.
